COURT’S OR JUDGE’S ORDERS
WPSB No.37 of 2026
Hon’ble Alok Mahra, J.
Mr. Lalit Samant, Advocate for the
petitioners.
Mr. Narain Dutt, Standing Counsel and 
Mr. S.M.S. Mehta, Brief Holder for the State of 
Uttarakhand.
2. Learned counsel for the State contends 
that the State possesses the authority to amend 
Service Rules, rendering such amendments 
immune from challenge by employees. To 
substantiate this position, reliance is placed on 
paragraph 10 of the Hon'ble Supreme Court's 
judgment in P.U. Joshi & Ors. Vs. Accountant 
General, Ahmedabad & Ors., reported in (2003) 
2 SCC 632.
3. In opposition, learned counsel for the 
petitioners asserts that vested rights accrued to 
the petitioners under the existing Service Rules 
cannot be divested by retrospective 
amendments thereto. This submission draws 
support from paragraphs 20 and 24 of the 
Hon'ble Supreme Court's decision in Chairman, 
Railway Board & Ors. Vs. C.R. Rangadhamaiah 
& Ors., reported in (1997) 6 SCC 623.
4. Admit. 
5. State may file counter-affidavit within four 
weeks. 
6. Within two weeks thereafter, rejoinder 
affidavit, if any, may be filed. 
7. List this on 27.04.2026 alongwith WPSB 
No. 2 of 2026. 
8. Heard on Interim Relief Application (I.A.
No. 1 of 2026). 
9. Learned counsel for the petitioners 
submits that in identical matter, this Court has 
stayed the operation of the impugned 
Government Order dated 18.12.2025.  10. This fact is admitted by the learned State 
Counsel. 
11. Having considered, till the next date of 
listing, the effect and operation of the impugned 
Government Order dated 18.12.2025, shall 
remain in abeyance.
12. The interim relief application stands 
disposed of accordingly.
13. Urgency application (I.A. No.2 of 2026) 
stands disposed of.
 
(Alok Mahra, J.)
 Vacation Judge 
 20.01.2026
Arpan
